component: Go golang.org/x/net/http2 (and the net/http HTTP/2 bundle), header frame reading
root_cause: After a header block passed MaxHeaderBytes, Framer.readMetaFrame stopped storing header fields but kept reading and HPACK-decoding every further CONTINUATION frame, with no cap on the excess frames or bytes before closing the connection, so a peer could make the endpoint decode unbounded header data for a request that would be rejected anyway.
notes: The same code is bundled into the Go standard library as src/net/http/h2_bundle.go (fixed in go1.21.9 and go1.22.2). The fix limits how much excess header data is processed and then closes the connection with a protocol error. Gap: no row asks what happens after a limit trips (G1).

root_cause: Each received PATH_CHALLENGE frame queued a PATH_RESPONSE in the general control-frame queue with no cap (and the frames were tracked for retransmission), while the peer could keep the queue from draining by collapsing the sender's congestion window and skewing its RTT estimate, so the queue grew until memory ran out.
notes: Fix spans two commits per release branch: #4199 caps queued PATH_RESPONSE frames at 256, #4200 stops retransmitting PATH_CHALLENGE and PATH_RESPONSE. Backports exist for v0.37.7, v0.38.2 and v0.39.4. The root package is flat, so the audit scope is the repository root package; the frame dispatch in connection.go was not checked by name. The seemann.io analysis is linked from the advisory and was not read.

classes: Consistency across sibling branches and similar entry points
root_cause: The Java parsers enforced the recursion limit on known message fields but not when merging or skipping unknown fields: nested groups handled as unknown fields (UnknownFieldSchema.mergeOneFieldFrom, ArrayDecoders.decodeUnknownField in the lite parser, CodedInputStream.skipMessage, and map field parsing) recursed without counting depth, so deep nesting overflowed the stack.
notes: Six backport commits (listed from OSV). The v28.2 release notes name ac9fb5b as the Java recursion check; the file and method list was read from the main-branch commit 4728531. Java versions 3.25.5, 4.27.5 and 4.28.2 are fixed. The java/core path prefix follows the repository layout and was not opened at the vulnerable ref.

root_cause: The streaming read paths (HTTPResponse.read(amt), read1, stream, read_chunked) passed each raw compressed chunk to the content decoder's decompress() with no output limit, so the decoder expanded the whole chunk at once whatever amount the caller asked for, letting a small, highly compressed body cause huge memory and CPU use in one call.
notes: The fix commit is a merge commit from a private fork; its first parent is the vulnerable main branch. The fix adds max_length to every decoder's decompress and requires Brotli 1.2.0 or later. The separate chained-encoding limit (CVE-2025-66418) was fixed in the same release and is a different root cause.

component: libexpat, incremental parsing of large tokens
root_cause: When one token needed several buffer fills, XML_Parse, XML_ParseBuffer and XML_ResumeParser re-ran the tokenizer from the start of the unfinished token on every new chunk, so total parsing work grew with the square of the token size.
notes: The fix (merge of PR #789, 16 commits) adds callProcessor with a reparse-deferral heuristic: a partial token is not parsed again until the available data has grown enough (confirmed in xmlparse.c at R_2_6_0). The heuristic can be turned off with XML_SetReparseDeferralEnabled. Gap: no row asks about re-scanning already-seen input across incremental calls (G2).

component: Node.js / V8, string table hashing of integer-like strings
root_cause: V8 hashed strings that look like small array indexes by storing their numeric value directly in the hash field instead of passing them through the seeded string hash, so their hash values were fixed and predictable and an attacker could make many keys collide in the string table (reached for example through JSON.parse).
notes: Fixed in Node.js v20.20.2, v22.22.2, v24.14.1 and v25.8.2. Commit 089d6c7 backports the V8 change (seeded array-index hash, 31 files) and enables v8_enable_seeded_array_index_hash; 6fae244 enables the flag and adds a test on another line. The release line of each commit was not checked. The changed file list was read; the diff lines were not. The upstream V8 changes are Gerrit CLs 7564330 and 7609720 (named in the Node.js post; not opened). Also give the audit deps/v8/src/objects/string-table.cc.

root_cause: TlsListener::poll_accept stopped polling the underlying TCP listener once pending TLS handshakes reached max_handshakes (default 64), and each slot could be held until the 10-second handshake timeout by a client that sends nothing, so a few idle connections per second blocked every other client from being accepted.
notes: Affects 0.9.1; fixed in 0.10.0. The fix is a merge commit; its first parent is the vulnerable main branch. After the fix the listener keeps accepting in batches (DEFAULT_ACCEPT_BATCH_SIZE) even when no handshake is ready, instead of stopping at a handshake cap.

root_cause: A WebSocket close completed only when the peer's close frame was read, and WsSession had no close timeout, so a connection whose reads the server had suspended with the suspend/resume feature, or whose client never finished the close, stayed open with its resources; the fix adds a session close timeout checked from WsWebSocketContainer.backgroundProcess.
notes: Fixed in 11.0.0-M17, 10.1.19, 9.0.86 and 8.5.99. The commit message names the suspend/resume case; the advisory says only that a WebSocket client could keep a connection open. The fix adds DEFAULT_SESSION_CLOSE_TIMEOUT (30 s) and WsSession.checkCloseTimeout.

component: SoftEtherVPN, IPsec over UDP (L2TP/IPsec NAT-T port)
root_cause: ProcIPsecEspPacketRecv answered every UDP-encapsulated ESP packet that matched no IPsec SA with two packets (an INVALID_SPI informational exchange and an IPsec SA delete), both larger than the request, sent to the unverified source address, so the server reflected and amplified spoofed traffic.
notes: Amplification factor about 2.75x per the advisory. Fixed in 5.02.5185; the fix drops packets with no matching SA (citing RFC 4303). src/Cedar is very large, so the audit scope is the IKE/IPsec file; give Proto_IPsec.c too if the audit needs the calling context. Hit only because a VPN routes to 4.28 (see note W4).

component: ISC BIND 9, TSIG handling in DNS messages
root_cause: For a TSIG with an unknown algorithm, the key created during verification had a NULL algorithm name (namefromalg gives NULL for unknown algorithms), and the error-reply path (spacefortsig in message.c, reserving room for the TSIG in the reply) passed that NULL name to dns_name_toregion, whose REQUIRE assertion aborted named.
notes: Affects 9.20.0 to 9.20.8 and 9.21.0 to 9.21.7; fixed in 9.20.9 and 9.21.8. The fix commit was read on the GitHub mirror; which branch it is on was not confirmed. The fix stores the algorithm as an enum in the key, adds dns_tsigkey_algorithm(), and skips dns_name_toregion in spacefortsig when the algorithm is unknown. lib/dns is large; message.c and tsig.c with their headers are enough for a focused audit.
